2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are that respondent Nos. 1-10 herein as the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 01 of 1986 in the Court of District Judge, Tangail, against the petitioner and proforma respondent No. 11 herein impleading them as the defendant and the proforma defendant respectively. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that long before the settlement operation, the villagers of Gandina Hindu Community established a temple and set up the image of Sree Sree Shashan Kalimata and had been performing religious rites. During settlement operation, some lands were recorded in the name of ex-landlord but in the remark column "Kodaldoha Kalibari by the Hindu Community" was shown as the possessor. Subsequently, with a view to removing complication that might arise in future, Abinash Chandra Ghosh and others executed a deed of endowment on 01.09.1947 in favour of the Sree Sree Shashan Kalimata. The local Hindu Community had been performing religious rites there. The villagers appointed defendant No. 1 as 'Shebait' for the management of the properties of the deity and to perform other religious rites. During the last settlement operation, the suit lands were recorded in the name of Abinash Chandra Ghosh and others. Consequently, the Shebait filed Miscellaneous Case No. 338 of 1968 under section 143A of the State Aquisition and Tenancy Act, which was allowed and the Revenue Authority was directed to record the suit lands in the name of deity. The Shebait was not performing the religious rites regularly and he did not maintain the accounts of the deity's property and misappropriated the entire usufructs of the property. Subsequently, the plaintiffs appointed one Santosh Kumar Chakraborty as the pujari of the deity for performing religious rites. Later, defendant No. 1 removed the image of the deity from the suit lands and converted the suit property into his personal property. Being aggrieved, the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 01 of 1986 for removal of the defendant as Shebait of the suit land and for appointing Shantosh Kumar Chakraborty as the pujari of the deity. 

 3. The petitioner herein as the defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that the plaintiffs do not have locus standi for filing the suit as they are believers of worshipping Vishnu and they are not entitled to offer Shashan Kali Puja not to speak of appointing as Shebait of the deity. After that, the defendant raised another question that there is no legal evidence about mismanagement and/or misappropriation of the deity's property and his further point is that since the plaintiffs and other villagers are not entitled to perform Shashan Kali Puja the suit is barred under section 15 of the Religious Endowments Act, 1863. The last point agitated by the defendant is that the suit property is not the trust property of the deity and the suit is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 8. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate, the impugned judgment and the materials on record, Having considered recitals of the deed endowment (Exhihit-3), the High Court Division came to a finding that this deed clearly disclosed that the Deity is the public debutter estate which is being used as such for many years by the members of the Hindu community. The High Court Division further held that a shebait who is guilty of misconduct or abuses his position as a trustee could be removed by the Court in a proper judicial proceeding.
